heading: Graph as a dictionary
body:
An **adjacency list** maps each node to its neighbors.

```python
adjList = {
  1: [2],
  2: [1, 3, 4],
  3: [2, 4]
}
```

Look up neighbors in **O(1)** — essential for DFS.

heading: Visited set stops infinite loops
body:
Graphs have cycles — unlike trees. Track visited nodes:

```python
visited = set()
if node in visited:
    return
visited.add(node)
```

Without this, DFS loops forever.

label: Build & DFS · Python

q: Why do we need to add edges in both directions when building an adjacency list for an undirected graph?
options: Because each edge connects both nodes bidirectionally, so both nodes must list each other as neighbors
To make the graph easier to visualize
To improve time complexity of DFS
explain: Undirected edges mean both u→v and v→u, so both must appear in the adjacency list.
